section_name: Additive Prediction Correction and Constant Residual Analysis

candidates.title: Fitting Regression Models with No Intercept Term
candidates.reason: Analyzes the foundational statistical consequences of omitting an intercept term in linear models, establishing that the residual sum and mean do not equal zero when a true non-zero offset exists, leading to systematic constant bias in predictions.

candidates.title: Regression through the Origin
candidates.reason: Presents a clear pedagogical derivation of the mechanics of no-intercept models, illustrating how forcing predictions through zero creates persistent residual offsets and distorts conventional goodness-of-fit metrics.

candidates.title: Leverage and Regression Through the Origin
candidates.reason: Examines the geometric and structural leverage imposed on a predictor when an intercept is omitted, providing key context for understanding how an unmodeled scalar offset influences residual behavior across data points.

candidates.title: Errors in Computer Packages. Least Squares Regression Through the Origin
candidates.reason: Demonstrates how omitting a constant term disrupts the standard zero-mean residual assumption, causing miscalculated sums of squares and misleading diagnostic statistics in software evaluations.

candidates.title: Cautionary Note about R2
candidates.reason: Examines the severe pitfalls and invalid interpretations of the coefficient of determination when applied to models that omit an intercept or leave uncorrected constant residual offsets.

candidates.title: Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine
candidates.reason: Formalizes the principle of additive prediction correction, proving that the optimal initial base predictor under squared error loss is a constant scalar offset matching the sample mean residual before any functional adjustments are added.

candidates.title: Generalized Additive Models
candidates.reason: Establishes the additive modeling framework wherein predictors are refined iteratively via residual estimation, centered on an explicit global intercept offset.

candidates.title: The Use of Model Output Statistics (MOS) in Objective Weather Forecasting
candidates.reason: Introduces the classic methodology of post-processing fixed physical model outputs with an additive linear regression correction to remove systematic mean residual bias.

candidates.title: Bias Correcting Climate Change Simulations - A Critical Review
candidates.reason: Provides a comprehensive critical review of additive mean offset corrections applied to fixed model predictions, evaluating underlying assumptions, estimation protocols, and the risks of assuming correction validity outside observed conditions.

candidates.title: Estimating the Error Rate of a Prediction Rule: Improvement on Cross-Validation
candidates.reason: Analyzes the phenomenon of in-sample optimism, explaining why evaluating a fitted adjustment—such as an estimated mean offset correction—on the exact training observations from which it was derived yields an unrealistically optimistic assessment.

candidates.title: Cross-Validatory Choice and Assessment of Statistical Predictions
candidates.reason: Formulates foundational principles of out-of-sample assessment, clarifying the statistical limits of testing an additive correction on the same small sample used for estimation.

candidates.title: Accurate Uncertainties for Deep Learning Using Calibrated Regression
candidates.reason: Investigates post-hoc recalibration protocols for fixed continuous predictors to align systematic residual misalignments and global offsets without retraining the base model.
